origins: Betrayal by a parent, spouse, friend, church leader, or institution can convince us that everyone will eventually hurt us. We keep people at arm’s length. Safe, but alone.
teaches: “Cursed is the man who trusts in mankind… But blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, whose confidence is in Him.” “It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in man.” Yet Scripture also shows trustworthy people: “Two are better than one,” and “As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.” Jesus told His disciples, “be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.” Trust is not all or nothing. It can be given in small steps, to people who show themselves reliable, while our deepest trust rests in God.
self_statements: If I trust, I will be hurt.
I will never open up again.
errors: Believing people are either fully trustworthy or not at all.
Feeling hurt and concluding that no one is safe.
Predicting that I will be hurt again.
questions: Who betrayed my trust, and what happened?
Has anyone proven reliable, even in small ways?
What would trust in small steps look like?
What do I lose by trusting no one?
What does Scripture say about trusting God and people?
Who could help me heal from the betrayal?
truth: Some people hurt me, but not everyone will. My deepest trust belongs to God, who never fails, and I can give trust slowly to those who prove reliable. Healing makes room for safe relationships.
hw_truths: Taking refuge in the Lord is better.
Trust can be given in small steps.
log: Each week, note one small trust you tried and how it went.
actions: Write what happened and how it affected you.
Note anyone who has proven trustworthy.
Share something small and watch the response.
prayer: Lord, I was hurt, and trusting is hard. You never fail. Heal my heart, give me discernment, and bring safe people into my life. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “It is better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in man.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I can't trust anybody.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
